Indo-Chinese Alliance for Chemical Fibres 
*542.    SHRI GHULAM NABIAZAD : † 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY : 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS-AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to 
state : 
(a) whether China is looking for technological alliances with Indian 
Corporates in the areas of Chemical Fibres; 
(b) if so, whether the prospects of collaboration between the two countries 
are very good; 
(c) whether the President, China Chemical Fibres Association has pointed 
out that there is a potential for information regarding markets between the two 
countries; 
(d) if so, whether any agreem ent in this regard has been reached between 
India and china for alliance in chemical technology; 
(e) if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) the steps being taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI 
SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA) : (a) to (0 A statement is laid on the Table of 
the House.

RAJYA SABHA [3 May. 2002] 
Statement 
There has been no formal proposal fr om Chinese side for technological 
alliances in chemical fibres. 
A delegation led by the President of th e China Chemical fibres Association 
attended the 4th International Conference organized by the Asian Chemical 
Fibre Industries Federation in Mumbai on 22nd and 23rd March, 2002. The 
President of the China Chem ical Fibres Association mentioned in his address 
that there is scope for exchange of views on topics of mutual interest including 
exchange of information and cooperation among the Asian, European and and 
American Chemical fibre Industries. 
SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD : Sir, accor ding to the hon. Minister, there 
has not been any proposal from the Chinese side for technological alliances 
between India and China in so far as chemical fibre is concerned. Also, 
according to the reply given by the hon. Minister, the Presid ent of the China 
Chemical Fibres Association while he was here in the month of March, 2002, 
had mentioned that there is a lot of scope for exchange of views on topics of 
mutual interest, including exchange of information and cooperation among the 
Asian, European and American chemical  fibre industries. I would like to ask 
the hon. Minister whether the Governme nt of India is aware that China has 
become the net importer of chemical fibr e and the same is the position of the 
USA and Europe. Is it not true that India has not been able to take advantage 
of the supply gap inspite of the fact that the country possesses the required 
technology, the requisite technology, and capability to produce chemical fibre. 
I would also like to know from the hon. Minister this. Is it not true that we 
have killed our chemical fibre companies ourselves, expect one or two most 
favoured ones? therefore, my question to the hort. Minister would be, what 
steps shall the Government of India take to take advantage of the huge 
demand-supply gap in China in chemical fibre and ensure a win-win situation 
for both the countries by achieving agreements and cooperation in this field 
and also build requisite companies with capacities within the country?

* 550. SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE

sion of agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes;

* 55l. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY:  Will the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Department of Science and Technology has developed the 
technology to recover fuel from the municipal solid wastes, on a pilot scale; 
(b) whether the Technology Informa tion, Forecasting and Assessment-
Council has identified a suitable.industrial partner in Bangalore for the same; 
(c) if not, whether Government would take steps to commission, a plant in

THE MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (DR. MURLI 
MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (d) The Department of Science and Technology 
(DST) successfully demonstrated the tec hnology to recover fuel pellets from 
Municipal Solid Wastes on a pilot scale level in Deonar dump yard near 
Mumbai with technomanagerial support from Technology Information Fore-
casting and Assessment Council (TIFAC). The pilot scale fuel pelletisation 
plant with total indigenous efforts was engineered, procured, erected and 
establised at a production rate of 2 Tonnes per Hour of fuel pellets having a 
calorific value of about 3000 Kcal/Kg. The process of conversion of garbage 
into fuel pellets involves primarily drying, separation of none combustibles, 
size reduction and pelletisation. A commercial scale plant for processing 700 
Tonnes per day of Municipal Solid Wastes to produce about 210 Tonnes per

Hyderabad (Andhra Pradesh) with the said technology with techno-manage-
rial support from TIFAC and financial support from the Technology Devel-
opment Board.

disseminated by TIFAC and DST. TlFAC's main task is to assess emerging 
technologies and create a few viable demonstrable models. It is for industries 
to establish similar plants elsewhere in coordination .with the concerned 
municipalities. The Karnataka Government has not sought Central Govern-
ment's assistance in establishing commercial-scale plants in that State.

(c) and (d) Large number of vacancies at the field level, inadequate mobility 
and fire arms, lack of expertise in the field of intelligence gathering, investigation 
and prosecution have been found to be the main bottle-necks in the effetive

70 

[3 May, 2002] RAJYA  SABHA 
Statement 
Salient features of the Wildlife Conservation Strategy-2002 adopted by the. 
Indian Board for Wild-life. 
1. Wild-Life and forests shall be declared priority sector at the national level 
for which' funds should be earmarked. 
2. Law enforcement agencies must ensure that those engaged in poaching, 
illicit trade in wild-life and wild-life products, destruction of their habitat, 
and such other illegal activities are given quick and deterrent punishment. 
3. The potential in wildlife tourism should be fully tapped, taking care that it 
does not have adverse impact on wild-life and protected areas. The revenue 
earned from increased tourism should be used entirely to augment available 
resources for conservation. 
4. No diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes from critical and 
ecologically fragile wild-life habitat shall be allowed 
5. Lands falling within 10 km of the boundaries of National Parks and 
Sanctuaries should be notified as Eco-fragile zones under section 3(v) of 
the Environment (Protection) Act and Rule 5 Sub-rule 5(viii) & (x) of the 
Environment (Protection) Rules. 
6. Removal of encroachments and illegal activities from within forestlands 
and Protected Areas. 
7. Settlement of rights in National Parks and Sanctuaries should not be used 
to exclude or reduce the areas that are crucial and integral part of the wild-
life habitat. 
8. More than 2000 vacant posts in the frontline staff of Protected Areas shall 
be filled immediately and provided basic infrastructure for efficient 
discharge of duties. Ban on recruitment of staff against vacant post should 
be lifted on lines with the Police Department.

tiger on Bazee com in No vember, 2001 for Guinness book of records for 
having largest tiger skin. The Regional Deputy Director, Wild Life Preservation,

Nath Tagore, India's famous Noble Laureate, which was vested in the Viswa

107 

RAJYA SABHA [3 May, 2002]

plagiarism and distortion of Tagore's works, the Bengal Intelligentsia had 
appealed to the Union Government to ask the United Nations Educational, 
Social and Cultural Organisation (UNESC O) to declare Tagore's works as 
world heritage; and 
(c) the action, if any, taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SMT.) RITA VERMA]: (a) Yes Sir

non-teaching staff, playground, dining  hall, library and laboratories etc. 
Arrangements are also made for internal  roads, water supply, electricity and 
other requirements. However, for hilly areas the designs of the buildings are

Details of the Schemes being implemented by DWCD at present 
1.  Scheme of Creches/Day Care Centres for Children of Working and ailing 
Women.  
It aims to provide day care services for the children (0-5 years) of mainly 
casual, mirgrant, agricultural and construction labourers. 
2. National Creche Fund 
It provides for a corpus fund to meet the growing requirement of opening 
more creche centers for working and ailing mothers. 
3. Hostels for Working Women 
Under the scheme financial assistance is given to voluntary organisations, 
local bodies and cooperative institutions engaged in the field of women's/ 
social welfare/women's education. Public Sector Undertaking, Women 
Development Corporations, Educational Institutions an State Governments for 
the construction of hostels for working women in order to enable women seek 
employment and participate in technical training. 
4. Setting up of employment-Cum-Training-Cum-lncome Generating units 
for Women (NORAD) 
Under this programme, financial assistance is given to Women's 
Development Corporations, Public Sector Corporations, autonomous bodies, 
and voluntary organisations, to train poor women, mostly in non-traditional 
trades and to ensure their employment in these areas. 
5. Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women (STEP) 
This Programme seeks to provide updated skills and new knowledge to 
poor and assetless women in the traditional sectors, such as, agriculture, 
animal husbandry,'dairying, fisheries, handlooms, handicrafts, khadi and village 
industries, sericulture, social forestry and wasteland development for enhancing 
their productivity and income generation. 
130 

[3 May, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
6. Short Stay Homes for. Women and Girls 
The Scheme seeks to protect and rehabilitate those women and girls who 
are facing social and moral danger due to family problems, mental strains, 
social ostracism, exploitation and other causes. 
7. Distance Education Programme 
The Scheme provides for a certificate course by IGNOU to train women Self 
Help group workers. 
8. Condensed Courses of Education & Vocational Training for women (CC 
&VT) 
The Scheme is implemented by the Central Social Welfare board with the 
objective of providing basic education and skills to needy women and also to 
benefit widows, destitute deserted women and also those belonging to 
economically backward classes. 
9. Awareness Generation Project (AGP) 
It aims to generate awareness among rural and poor women about their' 
status in the family and society and to activate them to work for achieving their 
rights and to deal with social issues. 
10. Scheme for women in Difficult Circumstances—Swadhar 
The scheme has been designed with a flexible and innovative approach to

(c) the countries in which the rights under the International Copyright 
Order, 1999 are applicable;

136 

[3 May, 20021 RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SMT.) RITA VERMA]: (a) and (b) The Copyright 
Office does not issue any no tification in respect of registration of copyright. 
The Copyright Office undertakes regist ration of copyrights in accordance 
with Section 45 of the Copyright Act, 1957, of different classes of works as 
defined under Section 13 of the Act. The particulars of the work eligible for 
registration are entered in the Register of Copyrights and relevant extracts of 
the same are sent to the applicant. The Copyright Office has entered particulars 
of a literary work titled "Y2K (Sankranti)" on the basis of an application under 
registration No. L-18402/99 dated 24.06.1999 in the name of Shri Shyam Singh 
Thakur of Bhopal and a copy of the entry in the Register has been furnished 
to the applicant. The idea contained in the literary work is not protected under 
the Copyright Act. It is the expression of an idea, which is protected under 
Copyright, and not the idea per se. In fact, the acquisition of copyright by the 
creator of a work is automatic and simultaneous with the creation of the work 
and it does not need any legal formality of registration etc. The registration of 
copyright does not grant the copyright owner any rights whatsoever other 
than what is already conferred under the Copyright Act. The Register of 
Copyrights is a public document and can be inspected by any person on any 
working day during office hours. 
(c) and (d) There are no rights provided under the International Copyright 
Order (ICO) published by the Government in the Official Gazette under section 
40 of the Copyright Act, 1957. A list of countries is given in the Schedule 
attached to the Order. These countries are members of international 
conventions relating to copyrights of which India is also a member. As per the 
International Copyright Order, the works of the countries specified in the 
schedule enjoy Copyright protection in India. Likewise, countries listed in the 
schedule are obliged to proteci Indian works. The Order is revised from time 
to time and its copies are placed on th e Table of the House. No one can use a 
copyright work without the permission of the owner of the copyright, as this 
constitutes infringement of the copyright. However, certain exemptions for 
fair use are provided by the copyright acts whereby a work can be used 
without the permission of the copyright owner for such specified purposes. 
(e) and (f) Do not arise.

which recorded 360 seismic events.

4049. DR. ABRAR AHMED: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) what steps Government have taken to augment the security of 
passengers of Indian Railways; 
(b) whether compensation to victims of rail accidents has been increased;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): (a) Maintena nce of law and order over the 
Railways is the responsibility of the State Governments which they discharge 
through their Government Railway Police (GRP). In addition to various 
mesures being taken by the GRP to improve the safety and security of the 
passengers, the Railway Administration is taking the following steps to assist 
GRP:— 
1. Anti-social elements are being re moved from railway premises and 
trains by RPF. 
2. Proper watch is being kept by Coach attendants/TEs on the passengers 
entering/detraining from the coaches  and the coaches are locked dur-
ing their run especially in night hours. 
3. FIR forms are made available with the Train Guards/Station Masters/ 
 
RPF to facilitate the travelling public to lodge their reports immedi-
ately. 
4. Sharing of Special Intelligence and Crime Intelligence between RPF 
and GRP is being done at all levels. 
5. Announcement through Public Address System and CCTV at 
important Railway Stations to alert the travelling passengers against 
theft to their belongings etc. 
6. Periodic co-ordination meetings with Government Railway Police and 
Local Police are being conducted to analyze the crime position on 
Railways with a view to take suitable preventive measures. 
7. Wherever the State Government wants to establish mobile post in the 
running trains, necessary facilities like accommodation etc. are being 
provided.

or untoward incidents taking place on or after 1-l 1-97. compensation for

well known International models on sporting awards for excellence, like the 
annual Laureus World Sports Awards, which recognise sporting excellence 
around the globe ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS (SHRI P. RADHAKRISHNAN): (a) Following are the highlights 
of major changes made especially those aimed at achieving greater 
transparency in the selection procedure :— 
(i)  Enlarged selection committee with more non-official members 
comprising of following :— 
• Sportsperson of eminence—Chairman 
• Olympians of eminence from different disciplines—5 Members 
• Arjuna Awardees from different disciplines—4 Members 
• Sports Administrators—2 Members 
• Director/Deputy Secretary (Sports), Ministry of Youth Affairs and 
Sports, Government of India—Member Secretary. 
(ii)  Excellence in performance at International level only will be taken 
into account for selecting the Awardees. 
(iii) The sportsperson found positive for use of drugs banned by the 
International Olympic Committee in any laboratory accredited by 
182 

[3 May, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
International Olympic Committee will not be eligible for Arjuna 
Award. 
(iv)  Maximum Number of Awardees has been fixed at 15 in any calendar 
year. 
(v) The prize money has been increased from Rs.   1.50 lakhs to Rs. 3.00 
lakhs. 
(b) Yes. Sir. 
(c) While finalizing the Scheme, the selection procedures followed by 
several Indian National Awards, were taken into account. No international 
models on sporting awards were taken into consideration. This Schemes has 
been devised keeping in view the Indian sports standards; as such no 
comparison can be drawn with international awards.

AND SPORTS (SHRI P. RADHAKRISHNAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir.

for life time achievement in sports. As the scheme is in draft stage, it is not 
possible to indicate the details at this stage.

MOTION ON PERSISTENCE OF VIOLENCE IN GUJARAT 
SHRI ROBERT KHARSHIING (Meghalaya) : Mr. Chairman, Sir, I rise 
to support this Motion. I th ank you for giving me this opportunity to make my 
maiden speech here in Rajya Sabha. I feel  it a great privilege to be able to 
express myself in this august House. Sir, today, we are discussing, continuing 
from yesterday, the tragic ev ents that took place in Gujarat. I wish to join my 
esteemed colleagues from both sides of the House, who have condemned the 
incidents first in Godhra and the subsequent revenge killings, rape and torture, 
especially, of the minorities, women and children in other parts of Gujarat. I 
also join other hon. Members who have deplored the terrible loss of property, 
homes and business establishments. Sir, yesterday, Madam Chairperson 
expressed her anguish by saying that if we cannot have peace in this House, 
how can we bring peace to Gujarat an d other parts of t he country. I humbly 
share her sentiments. Yesterday, I sat till the House adjourned at 12.00 p.m. 
There were several occasions when I wanted to leave the House. Such was 
my frustration at the leve l of the debate in the House. But there were three 
rays of light for me. First, when the L eader of the House, Mr. Jaswant Singh, 
announced the Government's decision to support the Motion. I feel that that 
one move defused a lot of tension. I t hank them for that. Secondly, when Dr. 
Manmohan Singh apologised to Madam Chairperson for some avoidable 
remarks made by others. I salute him for his humility. Thirdly, when my good 
senior friend, Mr. Nilotpal Basu, was in the Chair. Here, on the floor, he is a 
captain, but there in the Chair, he becomes a General. I wish he sits more 
often in the Chair.   He is better suited there, no pun intended. 
Now, I come to the situation which is prevailing in Gujarat. How can 
we bring peace, forgiveness and reconciliation there? Sir, as a new Member, I 
can only share my own experience. Sir, I was a radical - a 
205 

RAJYA SABHA [3 May, 2002] 
radical student leader. In 80's, as pres ident of the local students' union in 
Meghalaya, and General Secretary of the Meghalaya Students' Union, I used 
to instigate boys to beat up and harass people of other communities. Dislike 
and often hate for other communities and religions filled me. I was no different 
from those who committed those horrible cr imes in Gujarat. A great leader of 
Meghalaya, late Mr. Stanley Nichols Roy,  a Cabinet Minister there, helped me 
to change my behaviour. He taught me to listen to my inner voice, 'the antar 
atma'. It was difficult in the beginning, but I obeyed and persisted. 
Today, in my heart and mind, I embrace everyone, no matter what the 
colour, race, religion, caste or backgro und. I wish the sa me for Gujarat and 
India. I wish - for Gujarat and India which is at peace within itself, and a 
peacemaker among the nations of the world - I wish to say sorry for what I had 
done in my youth. I repeat I wish to sa y sorry to those of other communities 
against whom I have instigated hate. Sir, I sincerely hope that we, as a House, 
regardless of political affiliations, can apologise both to those who lost loved 
ones in Godhra, and to those hundreds  of other minorities, women and 
children who were raped, killed and driven out from their homes. But we in the 
Opposition, cannot point fingers at the other side, unless we ourselves 
apologise for the killings, rape and burning of thousands of Sikhs in 1984, and 
for the ongoing killings in the North-East, which started in the 1950s. In the 
1950s, Sir, Mizoram and Nagaland were even bombed by the Government of 
India. The Government of the day deni ed it, but the Naga and Mizo friends 
brought bombshells to display to us in Shillong. Maybe, an apology has been 
given, though I have not seen it. If it is sincere, why not repeat it? If over 5000 
Sikhs were killed, why can we not make many apologies? When the 
Australian, Prime Minister said sorry to the aboriginal people for the crimes 
committed ,by so-called Christian Whites, it did not make him less; it enhanced 
his prestige. When the New Zealand Prime Minister said sorry to the Maories 
for the wrongs and injustices committed ag ainst them, it helped heal some of 
the wounds and promoted national unity in  New Zealand. Sir, this I leave it to 
the individual conscience.  Sir, may I make the following suggestions? 
Sir, my first suggestion is that an all-party committee be formed to 
ensure communal harmony and peace in Gujarat and all over India. I support 
the suggestion made by an honourable Member from the Treasury Benches 
that the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition lead an all-party team 
to Gujarat.   I am also happy at the suggestion made by the 
206 

[3 May, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
same Leader of the Opposition for reconc iliation, and the favourable response 
I heard from the.Prime Minister. There is already a Foundation for communal 
harmony headed by the hon. Home Minister of the country. That could be 
activated by making it an all-party, or, a new all-party committee could be 
formed.   I leave it to the wisdom of senior leaders. 
My second suggestion is, Sir, that relief and rehabilitation 
programmes be handed over to an eminent NGO acceptable to the victims 
and minorities. Or, a temporary Task-Forc e be set up at the Prime Minister's 
Office to expedite and oversee relief works in Gujarat. 
Sir, allow me to conclude my maiden speech on a personal note. I 
am extremely happy to sit in this prestigious House. But I am sad that we 
wasted almost Rs. 1 crore a day during the recent standoff on Gujarat in both 
the Houses. Of course, both sides will blame the other group. I personally 
resolve that during my six years here, I will never shout, yell, enter the Well of 
the House or disrupt the proc eedings of ,the House. I be lieve, Sir, that if I am 
intolerant to another's point of view, if I refuse to listen to another, I am 
behaving with the same intolerance as those who committed those crimes in 
Gujarat. What example am I setting for the nation, if I am unable to 
understand or even hear the other's viewpoint. However, as I am a human 
being, I may make mistakes during these six years, in the heat of the moment. 
I request all of you, my senior colleagues here, to correct me whenever I do 
so.   I shall be grateful for that. 
Sir, I will strive to speak the truth in this House. I will strive to rise 
above party lines, and I will strive to build consensus in this House. 
Thank you very much, Sir, for giving me time to speak on such an 
important issue.

the State of Gujarat for over two deca des, I must confess that I will be

healthcare, drugs and pharmaceuticals and areas of e-entertainment are

political focus, rather than those with  purposeful economic focus.  The debate

set up, why should the basic agenda for development and eradication of 
poverty be deferred, year after year, and made subservient to political

forgetting that it is our duty to create a better future not for ourselves, but for 
the children of India.

Government that can balance the many  apparently conflicting demands and 
decide on how to execute our vision for the future. These are the very basics 
of good governance that will visibly set benchmarks of progress with multiple 
dimensions and, slowly but surely, stimulate the minds of those misguided and 
frustrated people, who have nothing better to do than indulge in acts of

SHRI B.J. PANDA (Orissa) : Madam  Deputy Chairman, I thank you 
for giving me this opportunity to express deep anguish on behalf of my party 
and on behalf of the people of Orissa for what has been happening in Gujarat 
for the last two months. I will stay within  the time-limit that has been allotted to 
me, because I can't contribute to this debat e by the quantity of my submission, 
nor can I express as heartfelt feeli ngs, as have been expressed by many 
Members of this august House, for instance, by Shri Ahmed Patel from Gujarat 
and by Shri Ram Jethmalani, who has spent time in the refugee camps. 
But I can say that the incidents in Gujarat have become a national 
shame, not just in the eyes of the Pr ime Minister, but the eyes of everybody 
involved in the NDA Government, of every citizen of this country. Certainly, I 
speak for the citizens of Orissa. When I ta lk about the incidents of Gujarat, we 
speak of all the incidents in Gujarat. What happened at Godhra should never 
be forgotten when we talk about the cont inuing violence that is going on in 
Gujarat even till now. What had happened at Godhra was despicable. Who 
was responsible for Godhra? Certainly, not the innocent men, women and 
children who have been slaughtered thereafter in Gujarat. This lawlessness 
that has taken over, this regula r and repeated mobocracy which has 
overwhelmed the police and the authorities - I say overwhelmed, Madam — I 
do not point finger because enough fingers have been pointed. But this is bad 
enough that this mobocracy has ov erwhelmed the system in Gujarat 
repeatedly and it continues to happen. I, therefore, endorse all the suggestions 
that have been made for the Centre to effectively intervene. Since, we have 
limited time, I would like to touch only one more aspect which has been 
debated here in this august House and which has been debated everywhere 
else, including the media - the role of the media itself. A lot of allegations have 
been made about the  media provoking the situatio n, about the media pouring 
oil, fanning flames of the situation. Madam, I would like to put forward that, yes, 
we have seen very gruesome sights particu larly on the electronic media, very 
graphic sights of what has been happening in Gujarat. But what we must 
understand is that this is not a production from Bollywood. This is a real life 
and this is happening. When we criticis e the media for showing these things, 
we must understand what exactly we are saying. Are we accusing them of bias 
or only sensationalism? If it is only s ensationalism that we are talking about, 
perhaps, there is some merit in what we say. But what do we do about it? But 
trying to curb sensationalism is tantamount to bringing in censorship to the 
media.   If there are provable cases of bias by the media, certainly, we

should take action. But trying to curb sensationalism in the media has never 
worked. It would not work now. It would not work ever in any democracy. I 
would also to say that the electronic me dia in a highly competitive form is still 
new to this country. It is only about ten-year-old that we have alternative 
electronic media in our homes from the sky. This sort of imagery may be new 
to this country but the world has seen it. The world has seen it for 30 or 40 yers 
ago it Vietnam,, the world has seen it in  Afghanistan and world has seen it in 
the Gulf War. When we criticise the media, we must also keep in mind that the 
media is considered to be the fourth pillar of democracy. Who well have the 
other pillars acquitted themselves? ... (Interruptions)... I endorse that criticism. I

sensationalism. That is the distinction that I am trying to make. When we 
criticise a column of democracy, we mu st examine how well the other columns 
have acquitted themselves. How well have we acquitted ourselves? I was 
touched and I must say that I was hono ured to be a Member of this House, 
when I heard a new Member today, pointing out this fact, and, in fact, taking an 
oath that in his six years' term, he would never shout, never interrupt and 
never rush into the well of the House. 
I wish more of us would take such an oath and more of us would

to do justice, before we start commenting on other pillars.  Thank you.

person. The Central Government and th e State Govemrnent should be fully 
responsible for the happenings in Gujarat. They should be aware that they are 
answerable to the people of the nation at the time of
